question: What is the main goal of musculoskeletal rehabilitation?

options.A: To accelerate the natural clotting of fractured bones
options.B: To completely eliminate all chronic joint inflammation
options.C: To restore functional capacity and independence
options.D: To replace lost surgical muscle mass with scar tissue

explanation: Great job! Rehab is all about helping patients get back on their feet so they can do their daily activities and live independently.

question: Why is the nurse so important during a patient's rehabilitation phase?

options.A: Nurses perform the orthopedic surgeries required for joint repair
options.B: Nurses coordinate care, monitor responses, and manage daily complications
options.C: Nurses prevent clients from ever experiencing physical discomfort
options.D: Nurses legally prescribe all physical therapy movement protocols

explanation: You got this! As a nurse, you are the heartbeat of the healthcare team—watching vital signs, catching complications early, and keeping the recovery plan on track.

question: What is the main reason we help patients work on their range of motion during rehab?

options.A: To increase the resting blood pressure of the client
options.B: To permanently numb the nerves surrounding a painful joint
options.C: To double the physical size of damaged muscle fibers
options.D: To prevent joint contractures and keep tissues flexible

explanation: Spot on! Moving those joints gently stops them from freezing up or getting stiff so the patient can keep their flexibility.

question: A patient recovering from a leg fracture is frustrated and feels like giving up. Which rehabilitation goal addresses this?

options.A: Accelerating the bone fracture healing timeline
options.B: Eliminating the need for any future physical therapy
options.D: Replacing lost joint cartilage with synthetic tissue

explanation: Recovery is tough mentally too! Supporting patients emotionally and helping them cope is just as important as the physical exercises.

question: Which of these checks is a key part of a neurovascular assessment on an injured arm or leg?

options.A: Total daily fluid intake and urine output
options.B: Bowel sound frequency and abdominal tone

explanation: Well done! Neurovascular checks are all about blood flow, feeling, and movement. Checking pulses and capillary refill tells us if blood is reaching the fingers and toes.

question: Why would a nurse check out a patient's home environment before they are discharged?

options.A: To identify physical barriers and fall hazards before discharge
options.B: To determine the financial income of the household members
options.C: To verify if the client owns a television or radio
options.D: To inspect the structural plumbing and electrical wiring

explanation: Safety first! Spotting dangerous things like loose rugs or stairs beforehand helps prevent nasty falls when they finally get home.

question: What do we call the exercise where the nurse moves the patient's joint for them, without the patient doing any work?
explanation: Correct! 'Passive' means the patient is relaxed while you do the moving to keep their joints nice and flexible.

question: Why must nurses strictly follow the doctor's weight-bearing orders during mobility training?

options.A: To prevent the client from building too much muscle too quickly
options.B: To protect healing bones and surgical repairs from excessive stress
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobility equipment
options.D: To ensure the client does not burn an excessive number of calories

explanation: Spot on! Putting too much weight on a healing bone or fresh surgery too soon can mess up the repair and cause setbacks.

question: When is the best time to give prescribed pain meds to a patient who is about to go to physical therapy?

options.A: Immediately after the therapy session has concluded
options.B: At breakfast time regardless of therapy schedules
options.C: Only when the client reports unbearable pain at night
options.D: About 30 to 45 minutes before the therapy session

explanation: Smart nursing! Giving meds ahead of time means the drug kicks in right when they are exercising, making therapy much more comfortable.

question: What is the main benefit of putting a cold pack on a fresh musculoskeletal injury?

options.A: Reducing acute inflammation and numbing localized discomfort
options.B: Stretching tight tendons before physical exercise begins
options.C: Permanently dissolving hardened scar tissue around the joint
options.D: Increasing local blood flow to speed up muscle contractions

explanation: You got it! Cold constricts blood vessels, which keeps swelling down and numbs the sharp pain right after an activity.

question: If a patient has weakness in their right leg, which hand should they use to hold their walking cane?
explanation: Correct! The cane always goes on the opposite side of the weak leg to give the best balance and support as they step.

question: What dangerous habit must nurses watch out for when patients use axillary crutches?

options.A: Resting body weight directly on the armpits
options.B: Looking straight ahead instead of down at the floor
options.C: Holding the handgrips too loosely with the palms
options.D: Walking too slowly during hallway exercises

explanation: Good catch! Resting weight in the armpits can smash nerves and blood vessels. Patients must always support their weight with their hands.

question: What is the main purpose of adaptive equipment in rehabilitation?

options.A: To help clients perform daily tasks independently despite physical limits
options.B: To monitor the daily vital signs of clients living at home
options.C: To speed up the biological knitting of broken bone fragments
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical therapy and exercise

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive tools give patients clever ways to wash, dress, and eat on their own without always needing help.

question: A patient recovering from a hip replacement cannot bend past 90 degrees. Which tool helps them put on shoes safely?
explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled shoehorn lets them reach their feet easily without breaking their hip movement rules.

question: Which symptom should a recovering patient at home report to their healthcare team right away?

options.A: Slow improvement in overall daily stamina
options.B: New numbness or tingling in the affected limb
options.C: Mild muscle soreness the day after exercise
options.D: Needing extra rest periods during afternoon chores

explanation: You nailed it! Numbness or tingling can mean a nerve is being squished or blood flow is blocked, so it needs a quick check.

question: Why is it so important to include family caregivers when teaching patients home care?

options.A: To teach them how to prescribe changes in physical therapy exercises
options.B: To train them to perform minor orthopedic surgeries at home
options.C: To legally transfer full medical responsibility of the client to them
options.D: To ensure they know how to support safe movement and spot warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Family members are the main helpers at home, so teaching them helps keep the patient safe and catches problems early.
